steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Don't your eyes get tired, staring at a book for so long?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I'm used to it.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: In my tournament days, my schedule was always packed. Time to myself was precious, so I often spent entire nights reading.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Don't feel pressured. You've only just returned to Leithanien.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Even in Kazimierz, I never forgot where my home was.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Over there, they called me 'The Knight from Leithanien.'

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: My Leithanian guests often discussed poetry and music from home with me, and praised me for being a paragon of 'the light of Leithanian elegance.'

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: They're not wrong.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Yet I spent most of my life away from this country.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: (Leithanian) Other than the language, and the books I've read...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: (Leithanian) How much do I truly know about this land?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Is there a pointy dome up ahead? What's the color of the tip?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: White, adorned with orange.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: It's my favorite flower shop. I can smell the flowers, but I wouldn't know if they've painted it a different color.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I envy you. You have a brand-new chance to appreciate this city, this country.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Unlike me, who's never had the opportunity to see Zwillingstürme with my own eyes.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Your eyes...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: My sight died with the Witch King, twenty-three years ago. That's the last time I saw the city.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Unlike me, you have a chance to see the beauty of the present, and... a future that should be better.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Hello, this is Droste.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...What did you say?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Sorry. I heard you. I just... couldn't believe what I heard.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Who is it?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The Gendarmerie who was a Candle Knight fan. I asked him to follow up on the art gallery incident.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Neither of us thought it would be a simple case.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But what I didn't expect was...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Loris Bordin, confirmed dead.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Cause of death is Originium Arts trauma from at least five different sources. Direct cause of death is believed to be suffocation caused by the ribcage penetrating the lungs.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The next step is to destroy the statue and retrieve the body.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Statue is believed to have been created by an extremely rare form of matter reconstruction Arts, and appears to be highly resistant to damage.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: Wait up, you're too fast—

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: What the hell are you doing?!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Loris Bordin was a citizen of Laterano.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Notarial Hall regulations dictate that I examine his body to ascertain whether he left behind an executable will.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: So you'll shoot the whole crime scene to pieces?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am quite accurate.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: My calculations indicate only a 27% chance that destroying the statue without damaging the body will cause a collapse.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: You can't.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Explain.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: First of all, the Gendarmerie has the area surrounded.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: They heard the gunshots, and will be in here in three minutes.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: When they do, they'll see you, a Sankta, pointing a gun at the mutilated body of their commander.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I'll be quick.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: I said, 'first of all'!

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: More importantly, there's no way you can retrieve Bordin's body intact. His flesh is a part of the statue now. They're completely inseparable—

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Not even with your Arts?

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: You didn't seriously think a kid like me could undo the Witch King's Arts, did you?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Over here!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It took them less than two minutes.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You should have mentioned your second point first. If there is excessive difficulty in completing the objective, then I will delay the retrieval of Loris Bordin's body.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: My bad. I didn't think there could possibly be anyone harder to communicate with than her.

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Put down your weapon! Turn around!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We're surrounded.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: I'll count to ten, then we make a run for it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your name.

steps.name: Serene Apprentice
steps.text: Name? Micha. Micha Wolf... Wait, now's not the time for introductions, is it?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You're attempting to persuade me to violate the laws of Leithanien. I must reassess the logic of continuing to work with you.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: We share a common goal. I want to find Arturia too. Is that enough?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But this is an international matter. His Holiness would want me to—

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: The culprit won't wait for the diplomatic process to finish.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What is the count at now?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: ...Ten. Let's just say it's ten. Go!

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: Frau Droste!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: What's the situation, Pym?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: The suspects fled the scene. A small Lupo with unusual Arts, and a gun-wielding Sankta. Must be the same one who broke into the art gallery.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: A Sankta and a Lupo?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Is that the crime scene?

steps.name: Gendarmerie
steps.text: I wouldn't advise heading into the sewers, meine Dame... It's not a sight for the faint of heart.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Bordin's footprints stretch from the entrance into this area.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The scent of Originium Arts... There was a big fight here.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: A statue in the shape of the Witch King's twisted horns. Not at all how the books describe them.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Wait, is that...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Herr Bordin's face? In the middle of the statue?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: How... how could they be so cruel?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...Who's there?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I know you're there. Show yourself.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Don't worry, I'm neither Gendarmerie nor secret police.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I'm just mourning for Herr Bordin, like you.
Did you know him?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Only in passing.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: When we first met, he reminded me of many people I've worked with in Kazimierz.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: People who once dreamt big dreams with a burning passion. But it's a rare soul that never wavers, always shining bright like a lighthouse.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Most are like Herr Bordin... or myself.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Which makes me all the more curious. What made him decide to face such a dangerous foe by himself?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And... why him?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Why kill such an ordinary man, one already resigned to his own mediocrity?

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: But he wasn't an ordinary man!

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: He was a hero! He came here to save lives... *sob*

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Do you need a handkerchief?

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: I'm sorry... I was so stupid... I'm the one who got him killed...

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: He told me to run, so I ran. But I should've known they wouldn't let him live!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Who exactly are 'they'?

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: I'm not so sure myself, all I know is that they all wear masks and call themselves the 'Echoes of Herkunftshorn.'

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...The name of the Witch King.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I've read that his followers believe that using his name grants them his wisdom and insight, even after his death.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: That's not just a legend! Didn't you see the statue they made from Loris's flesh? They're punishing traitors in his name!

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: They said that the soul of the traitor will lead them to the lost Genesis Horn.
The statue in the park comes alive.
It stands up, swinging its stone instrument like an executioner's axe, bringing it down on the people below.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Ah—!

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Look out!

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Th-That was close... did something crush the statue?! It's so dark...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...It's nothing.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Just never speak that name to anyone ever again.

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Herk... Herkun... could the legends really be true?

steps.name: Stubborn Apprentice
steps.text: Is it true that His Majesty isn't really dead, and that we still live under his gaze?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Try to forget everything you saw and heard these past few days... other than Herr Bordin's sacrifice.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: As an Empresses' Voice, I promise you that his death will not fade into silence.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Follow the light. My candle will protect you.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: ...The lost Genesis Horn? I've heard rumors.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Before he jumped from his spire following his liege's death, the Witch King's concertmaster claimed that Herkunftshorn... that the Genesis Horn still 'stands' somewhere on this land.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: At first, Their Majesties believed this to refer to the Spire of the Witch King.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But that Spire had long since been toppled.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Indeed. Their Majesties destroyed every brick and tile that could have contained the Witch King's Arts, and recombined them to form the bones and blood of the Twin Empresses' Spires.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The remnants believe that the Spire still exists, then?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Or maybe it's not a spire at all.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: In Leithanien, a spire is simply a symbol of one prowess in Arts.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: If your theory is correct, and there's some kind of ritual behind these deaths...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Then they must be looking for the final secret the Witch King left in this realm.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...'Death of the Witch King.'

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The theme of Frau Seemann's final painting.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: The Witch King's remnants do not pick their victims at random. Perhaps the secret they're looking for has something to do with her painting.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Their Majesties' casters have examined all the artwork in the museum and found nothing of note.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Perhaps she left other clues in the creation process.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Frau Löwenstein, please proceed to Frau Seemann's residence. I'll meet you there.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: You're going to walk the streets, just like that? Don't you know that the Gendarmerie are looking for you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It is more efficient to find Arturia before they catch up.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: You don't even care how big of a mess you make, do you? Just don't leave the cleanup to me.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You said we shared a common goal.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: I suppose.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: And you said that Arturia lured you away to target that officer.

spans.text: said that Arturia lured you away to target that officer.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: But why? Why give him a chance to fight back if she just wanted him dead?

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Is murder not enough for her? Does she enjoy watching people die in pain?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No, she takes no joy in hurting others.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Are you sure about that? She's hanging out with the Witch King's remnants. Why would you expect her to have basic morals?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Define morals.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If morals are a set of behavioral rules that ensure social order, then yes, Arturia is certainly a dangerous criminal with no regard for morality.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: However, if they represent the impetus and capacity to understand and respect the emotions and experiences of another, then I have never met an individual with more morals than her.

steps.name: Micha
steps.text: ...Get to the point.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Arturia did not intend to kill Loris Bordin.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That statue was an affront to life. She would have deemed it unbearably ugly.

steps.name: Old Noble Upstairs
steps.text: What's the commotion this time? Have those ignorant peasants come to cause trouble again?

spans.text: time? Have those ignorant peasants come to cause trouble again?

steps.name: Old Noble Upstairs
steps.text: Why do we give the Gendarmerie so many favors if they can't even do their jobs? Get me on the line with Bordin.

steps.name: Old Noble Upstairs
steps.text: What did you say? Bordin's dead?

steps.name: Old Noble Upstairs
steps.text: I knew the Gendarmerie were trash!

steps.name: Old Noble Upstairs
steps.text: This cello... not too bad. It sounds just like the one from a few days ago. No doubt this culturally rich alley has drawn the attention of a famous musician.

steps.name: Old Noble Upstairs
steps.text: Wings and a halo? My goodness, it's a Sankta from Laterano!

steps.name: Old Noble Upstairs
steps.text: I dread for the future of our dear Leithanien!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: This piece is dedicated to the return of the hero, Loris Bordin.
The tune of the cello echoes through the alley.
The moment the hero of days past rediscovered his courage, his suppressed love and hatred, regret and determination, hope and despair—all are revealed by its melody.
It is the sound of mourning, of remembrance, of praise.
The life that should have faded is brought back more brilliant than ever. Brighter than the morning sun, brighter than the blooming flowers.

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Frau Seemann's belongings have been sorted and laid out upstairs... Frau Löwenstein? Are you crying?

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I think I'm 'seeing' memories.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Are the marigolds in the alley blooming?

steps.name: Noble Attendant
steps.text: Yes. This was her favorite season. She used to lean by the window, painting the passersby.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Yes, I remember.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: I loved her paintings. My memories of them have never faded in color.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Those golden days, when we all lived with hope for the future...

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: But before you know it, it's all in the past.

steps.name: Cora
steps.text: Take me to Frieda's room, Anna.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Hello.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: You're back, Frau Droste. Of all the nobles I've met, I've never known a more avid reader.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I would like to access the library at the top floor.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: The top floor? The forbidden section?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I need to review the records of the forbidden research conducted by the Witch King's remnants in recent years.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: That might be an issue...

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: I can get Her Majesty's permission immediately, if necessary.

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: There's no need for that. Naturally, the forbidden section is open to an Empresses' Voice. However, I'm afraid that all the documents were removed this morning.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: ...May I ask who did it?

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: A spire caster. On Her Majesty's orders, as far as I know.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: But it was Her Majesty who gave me her blessing to come here...

steps.name: Spire Caster
steps.text: As you well know, there is more than one woman who bears that title.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: I hope you're ready. I won't tolerate any more interruptions to the plan.
Almost there. I just need these experiment notes.
You Leithanians have such awful hobbies. It's such a bother trying to sift something useful from all the chaff.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Gertrude Strollo was simply a convenient woman to set up to take the fall. Her talents were mediocre.
Did you involve every noble in this? Even the ones who had secret dealings with the Victorian dukes last time?

spans.text: noble in this? Even the ones who had secret dealings with the Victorian dukes last time?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Every one I could find.
A familiar tone.
No wonder they fear you so much, Your Majesty. Do you know what they call you behind closed doors? 'The next Witch King.' I have to say, your similar taste in wardrobe does you no favors either.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: I've never denied what Herkunftshorn's intelligence, skill, and strength meant to Leithanien.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: In fact, that's exactly what we need right now.
The Kurfürsten wouldn't like the sound of that at all.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: It's not the title of 'Witch King' that they fear. What they fear is Lieselotte and I walking Herkunftshorn's old path, and encroaching on their power and interests.
You remind me of old Leopold. When the two of you were born, he asked me what the life expectancy of children born of the eldritch arts was.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: And your answer?
I said, 'I can't give you a precise answer, Your Excellency the Großherzog, but I'm sure they'll outlive you.'

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: I doubt he was happy to hear that.
Was I wrong? He wanted to see the fall of Herkunftshorn, but forgot to take his own age into account.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Leopold participated in the Battle of the Four Emperors, and led the revolution that overthrew the Witch King. He was undoubtedly a hero of Leithanien.
Heroes can be greedy too.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Greed can be forgiven, as long as they stand for a unified Leithanien.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Otherwise, the greedy must be parted from their positions. Or their heads from their necks.
Ruling with an iron fist, I see. But what does Ewigegnade think about that?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Lieselotte does not approve of my methods. She whispers in my ear that such radical measures only create more opposition.
Hmph. She thinks herself the gentle mother.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Your words would sting her.
Grimmacht, my harsh Kaiserin, it is so unsettling to see such sentimentality on your face.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Lieselotte truly loves Leithanien and its people. As such, she is destined to stand in my way.
Good. Now there's the dark, brooding look I know and love.
Did you want to convince me that you'll be able to see it through when the time comes?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Many scholars believe that those born from Arts, like us, are born without a soul.
Tsk.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: They say the same of you. They believe that we are of the same kind.
Oh? For our lack of souls, or for our cruelty?

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: Help me one more time, Fremont.

steps.name: Grimmacht
steps.text: We must find the Witch King's legacy.
(Indistinct voice)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Someone... calling to me?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Was it... you?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Where's the one who saved my life?

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Dead.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'm sorry... Once again, I've let the courage of another go to waste.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...Nngh!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Water?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You poured water on my face?

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Drink.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're mistaken if you think I'll simply cooper—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ugh!

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: If you won't drink, I'll have to take other measures.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: *cough* *cough* Is this... medicine? Or some novel form of torture, Herr Executioner?

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Dying is easy, especially for a frail, Infected noble.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: But you have only one chance to do it.

steps.name: Stern Youth
steps.text: Before you die, think carefully about how you really want to make your curtain call.
